title: Order generators in an arbitrary near-point presentation
statement:
Let $F$ be a field of any characteristic and let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero reduced Noetherian local commutative $F$-algebra essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be a prime ideal, assume $A=R/I$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme], and assume that no minimal prime of $R$ contains $I$ (a minimal prime is a prime ideal containing no strictly smaller prime). Put $k=R/\mathfrak m$ and $S=(\operatorname{gr}_I R)\otimes_A k$, and assume $\operatorname{gr}_I R$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $Y=\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ and let $y\in Y$ lie over the closed point [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-nagata-affine-blowup]. Identify this fibre with $\operatorname{Proj}S$ [def-pc-proj]. Set $R_y=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n_y$, and set
$$h_R(n)=\operatorname{length}_R(R/\mathfrak m^{n+1}),\quad h_y(n)=\operatorname{length}_{R_y}(R_y/\mathfrak n_y^{n+1}),\quad \delta=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(y)$$
[def-weil-pbc-module-length, def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-weil-residue-field], and $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{j=0}^n f(j)$. Assume $\Lambda^\delta h_y=h_R$.
For any graded surjection $P=k[Z_1,\ldots,Z_N]\twoheadrightarrow S$, with variables of degree one, let $K$ be its homogeneous kernel and let $\mathfrak q_y\subset P$ be the inverse image of the homogeneous prime representing $y$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Then N is positive, q_y is homogeneous, prime and relevant, and K is the ideal generated by the homogeneous H in K of positive degree d for which H/1 belongs to (q_y P_(q_y))^d [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The prime on S is defined by the span of the canonical initial forms of the homogeneous Rees monomials belonging to the point y; no arbitrary fibre identification is chosen. This conclusion is only the numerical order-generation input, with no assertion about additive subgroups or translation action.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, Theorem IV; Dietel (2014), Theorem 9.2.2 and Lemma 9.1.8, pp.108--109. The minimal-presentation reduction and local-map argument are steps 1--3 of lem-trf-near-point-additive-symmetry. Canonical fibre identification: CJS Theorem 2.2(2)(ii). Agent reconstruction of the comparison glue, using the already stated nearBlowup_order_generators input.

proof.text: The canonical graded quotient Rees(I)/m Rees(I) identifies with S=k tensor_(R/I) gr_I R. The point prime contains m Rees(I) since y lies over m, and its quotient is homogeneous, prime and relevant. Its image is the ideal span of the initial forms of homogeneous Rees monomials in that prime: both inclusions follow by writing an element as a finite sum of its homogeneous pieces. Pull back along the given graded surjection. The resulting q is prime, homogeneous and relevant. If N=0, the positive-degree ideal of the source is zero and is contained in q, contrary to relevance.

The evaluation R -> k(y) from global coefficients equals the composite through the local ring at the closed point and the residue-field map of the blowup, by naturality of evaluation. Both vanish on m and induce the same homomorphism k -> k(y), as checked on quotient representatives. Hence their algebra structures and relative transcendence degrees agree, and the displayed near equality gives the hypothesis of nearBlowup_order_generators.

Reduce the given presentation to a minimal one. The degree-one map $P_1\to S_1$ is surjective: since the map is graded, the degree-one part of any preimage of an element of $S_1$ is a preimage. Choose a basis $V_1,\ldots,V_r$ of its kernel and lift a basis of $S_1$ to $X_1,\ldots,X_e$. The invertible linear change gives $P=k[X,V]=Q[V]$, $Q=k[X]$. Its inverse is the inverse matrix substitution, by the polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. The map $Q\to S$ is surjective because $S$ is generated by $S_1$ [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. With $J=\ker(Q\to S)$ and $\mathfrak q_0$ the inverse image of $y$, evaluation at $V=0$ shows $K=(V)+JP$ and $\mathfrak q_y=(V)+\mathfrak q_0P$: a polynomial minus its value at $V=0$ belongs to $(V)$. In particular the presentation $Q\to S$ has bijective degree-one map. Linear substitutions commute with addition, negation and evaluation at zero, so an ideal satisfying the desired formulas in $(X,V)$ coordinates gives one in the original coordinates by the inverse substitution.

Apply lem-trf-near-blowup-order-generators to the minimal presentation Q onto S. The prime q0 is specified on homogeneous representatives by the canonical Rees quotient; this is exactly its hq condition. Gradedness follows from the variables having degree one. The bijection on degree one is the basis construction. The algebra-structure comparison above transports hnear. The theorem gives J generated by its homogeneous positive-degree elements of local order at least their degree.

The inclusion $Q\to P$ induces a local homomorphism $Q_{\mathfrak q_0}\to P_{\mathfrak q_y}$: every denominator outside $\mathfrak q_0$ remains outside $\mathfrak q_y$, since $\mathfrak q_y\cap Q=\mathfrak q_0$. It takes $\mathfrak q_0Q_{\mathfrak q_0}$ into $\mathfrak q_yP_{\mathfrak q_y}$ and hence takes its $d$th power into the $d$th power, by multiplying fractions [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Thus each of the generators $H$ from Step 2 lies in $U_d$. Also each $V_i\in U_1$. Since $K=(V)+JP$, these $H$ and $V_i$ generate $K$ and are all in $U$. This only uses containment of powers under a local map; no equality of orders under a residue-field extension is assumed. The resulting generators H and V are among the displayed positive-degree order generators, and every displayed generator belongs to K by definition. These two inclusions give the equality. Undo the linear coordinate change: it gives an isomorphism of the corresponding local rings, preserving powers and homogeneous degrees.

theorem near_point_order_presentation
    {F : Type v} [Field F] {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsReduced R] [Algebra F R]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType F R]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) [I.IsPrime]
    [IsRegularLocalRing (R ⧸ I)]
    (hcomponents : ∀ p ∈ minimalPrimes R, ¬ I ≤ p)
    [Module.Flat (R ⧸ I) (Ideal.associatedGraded I)]
    (y : AffineBlowup I)
    (hy : AffineBlowup.toSpec I y = IsLocalRing.closedPoint R)
    (hnear : (summation^[(letI := ((((Spec (.of R)).residueFieldCongr hy.symm).hom ≫
        (AffineBlowup.toSpec I).residueFieldMap y).hom.comp
          (IsLocalRing.ResidueField.mapEquiv
            (stalkClosedPointIso (.of R)).symm.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv).toRingHom).toAlgebra
        Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R)
          ((AffineBlowup I).residueField y)))]) (localFunction (AffineBlowup I) y) =
      fun n : ℕ ↦ (Module.length R
        (R ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) ^ (n + 1))).toNat)
    (N : ℕ)
    (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin N) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) →ₐ[IsLocalRing.ResidueField R]
      Ideal.normalConeFibre I hI)
    (hφ : Function.Surjective φ)
    (hgraded : ∀ i : Fin N, φ (MvPolynomial.X i) ∈
      Submodule.span (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R)
        (Set.range (Ideal.normalConeFibreClass I hI 1))) :
    let q := Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom (Ideal.span {z | ∃ (n : ℕ) (a : (I ^ n : Ideal R)),
      reesMonomial I a.val a.property ∈ y.asHomogeneousIdeal.toIdeal ∧
        z = Ideal.normalConeFibreClass I hI n a})
    1 ≤ N ∧ ∃ hq : q.IsPrime,
      letI := hq
      (∀ f ∈ q, ∀ d : ℕ, MvPolynomial.homogeneousComponent d f ∈ q) ∧
      (¬ @HomogeneousIdeal.toIdeal _ _ _ _ _ _
        (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin N) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R)) _ _
        MvPolynomial.gradedAlgebra (@HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _
          (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin N) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R))
          MvPolynomial.gradedAlgebra) ≤ q) ∧
      RingHom.ker φ.toRingHom = Ideal.span
        {H : MvPolynomial (Fin N) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) | φ H = 0 ∧
          ∃ d : ℕ, 0 < d ∧ H.IsHomogeneous d ∧
            algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin N) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R))
              (Localization.AtPrime q) H ∈
                (q.map (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin N) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R))
                  (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ d}
